subject: Intermittent VPC route degradation impacting control-plane — next steps and post-incident follow-up
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: ops@clinicnova.com, sara.nguyen@clinicnova.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Observed VPC route degradation affecting control-plane connectivity (opaque route)

Hi Sara / ClinicNova ops team,

We observed an intermittent increase in control-plane RPC failures and reconnects from your private deployment's agents starting ~2026-05-17 08:10 PDT. Symptoms we see: repeated control-plane session resets, elevated error rate in the management channel, and a spike in route latency for the path we refer to internally as the "opaque route" (a transit path through our partner fabric).

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Put the canary upgrade that was rolling yesterday into rollback for your customer pool.
- Disabled the new path-selection policy that was part of the canary.
- Collected logs and a pcap for the time window (attached).

Can you confirm whether you saw any recent network changes on your side (firewall rules, BGP changes, or private peering adjustments) in the 07:30–08:30 PDT window? We'd like to set a 30-min bridge to correlate logs live — proposing 09:15 PDT if that works.

Attachments: privatelog_20260517.tar.gz (log bundle), pcap_opaque_route_0517.pcap

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin

Forwarding ClinicNova's confirmation and logs. Marcus — initial look at the pcap shows repeated TCP RSTs on the management channel and asymmetric TTLs. Can you triage routing/peer behavior with Acme Transit? Jordan, please prepare rollback notes and ETA for a maintenance window if needed.

-----Original message attached above-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clinicnova.com>, network@acme-transit.net
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:28:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observed VPC route degradation affecting control-plane connectivity (opaque route)

Summary of technical findings from initial triage:
- Root cause (provisional): transient BGP route propagation inconsistency on the Acme Transit fabric leading to an alternate intermediate hop dropping or resetting management traffic; this manifested as asymmetric return paths and TCP RST bursts.
- Evidence: captured pcap shows repeated three-way handshake failures followed by RSTs between Redwood agents and our control-plane endpoints; traceroutes from multiple agents diverge mid-transit.
- Immediate mitigation applied: rolled back the canary change that adjusted path selection and disabled ECMP steering we had enabled for the canary group. We also applied a short-term policy to prefer the stable peer path for ClinicNova's prefixes.

Next steps:
1) Work with Acme Transit (cc'd) to get their BGP logs for the 07:45–08:45 window.
2) Schedule a coordinated maintenance window to hard-pin stable routing for ClinicNova while Acme propagates a fix (recommended 2-hour window, low-traffic period).
3) Produce a full post-incident report with timeline and remediation actions (I will take ownership, target delivery: 2026-05-19 EOD).

Attaching an internal runbook fragment and the extracted netflow snippets.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alejandro Ramirez <network@acme-transit.net>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clinicnova.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 13:02:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed VPC route degradation affecting control-plane connectivity (opaque route)

Chloe / Marcus / Sara — Acme Transit ops here. We observed a brief RPKI validation failure on one of our exchange points that caused route withdrawal for a subset of prefixes for ~9 minutes (07:58–08:07 PDT). Customers on that exchange would have seen asymmetric routing until BGP converged. We're working with the exchange to harden validation and will publish a timeline after our internal review.

Logs attached: acme-exchange-logs-0517.tar.gz. We recommend the maintenance window Marcus proposed to pin routes while we complete the remediation.

—Alejandro
Acme Transit — Network Ops

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: ops@clinicnova.com, sara.nguyen@clinicnova.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alejandro Ramirez <network@acme-transit.net>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: ClinicNova incident wrap-up, timeline, and proposed next steps

Hi Sara / ClinicNova team — thanks again for the bridge earlier and for coordinating with Acme. This note closes the immediate escalation and lays out next steps and offers:

What happened (summary):
- 2026-05-17 07:58–08:07 PDT: transient RPKI validation failure at an exchange point used by Acme Transit caused route withdrawal for a subset of ClinicNova prefixes.
- The withdrawal produced asymmetric return paths and intermittent TCP RSTs for our control-plane connections, increasing reconnects and brief management interruptions.
- We rolled back the canary that changed path-selection behavior and applied a short-lived preference for the stable peer path to restore connectivity.

Impact:
- Control-plane reconnects for ~9 minutes, increased API management latency for the agents tied to your deployment. No persisted data loss; control-plane state recovered after route convergence.

Remediations completed:
- Canary rollback and policy revert (completed 08:15 PDT).
- Temporary routing preference enforced for ClinicNova prefixes.
- Requested and received Acme exchange logs; Acme will harden RPKI validation.

Planned follow-ups:
- Full post-incident report (SUP-1729) with packet-level timeline and recommended hardening: delivery 2026-05-19 EOD (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1729).
- Proposed maintenance window to pin stable routing for 2 hours next Thursday (2026-05-27 02:00–04:00 PDT) — please confirm availability.
- Offer: In recognition of impact, Redwood is prepared to apply a 10% service credit for the impacted billing period. If you agree, we will initiate the credit and send formal documentation.

Attachments: runbook-opaque-route-mitigation.pdf, privatelog_20260517.tar.gz

Would you like us to proceed with scheduling the maintenance window and the service credit paperwork?

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
